### Framework-agnostic app boundary with start()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/runtime-targets.md

Framework-agnostic app boundary example using plain Request and Response. Starts the onboarding workflow with a userId from the request body and returns the runId.

```ts
import { start } from 'workflow/api';
import { onboardingWorkflow } from '../workflows/onboarding';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const body = (await request.json()) as { userId: string };
  const run = await start(onboardingWorkflow, [body.userId]);
  return Response.json({ runId: run.runId });
}
```

--------------------------------

### Hono app boundary with start()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/runtime-targets.md

Named-framework app boundary example using Hono. Defines a POST route that starts the onboarding workflow and returns the runId as JSON.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { start } from 'workflow/api';
import { onboardingWorkflow } from '../workflows/onboarding';

const app = new Hono();

app.post('/api/onboarding/start', async (c) => {
  const body = (await c.req.json()) as { userId: string };
  const run = await start(onboardingWorkflow, [body.userId]);
  return c.json({ runId: run.runId });
});

export default app;
```

### Start Postgres World in SvelteKit hooks.server.ts

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/postgres.mdx

Create a src/hooks.server.ts file. This SvelteKit server init hook starts the Postgres World worker on server startup. The world.start?.() call is optional chaining because worlds that deliver work over HTTP (like Vercel World) have no worker to start.

```ts
import type { ServerInit } from "@sveltejs/kit";

export const init: ServerInit = async () => {
  const { getWorld } = await import("workflow/runtime");
  const world = await getWorld();
  await world.start?.();
};
```

### Start Postgres World in Nitro plugin and config

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/postgres.mdx

Create a plugin to start the world on server initialization, then register it in your nitro.config.ts. The plugin imports the runtime and calls world.start?.() to subscribe to the Postgres World queue. The config adds the workflow/nitro module and the plugin file.

```ts
import { defineNitroPlugin } from "nitro/~internal/runtime/plugin";

export default defineNitroPlugin(async () => {
  const { getWorld } = await import("workflow/runtime");
  const world = await getWorld();
  await world.start?.();
});
```

```ts
import { defineNitroConfig } from "nitropack";

export default defineNitroConfig({
  modules: ["workflow/nitro"],
  plugins: ["plugins/start-pg-world.ts"],
});
```

--------------------------------

### Start Postgres World in Next.js instrumentation.ts

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/postgres.mdx

Create an instrumentation.ts file in your project root. This registers a server startup hook that starts the Postgres World worker, but only when not running on the Edge runtime. The world.start?.() call is optional chaining because worlds that deliver work over HTTP (like Vercel World) have no worker to start.

```ts
export async function register() {
  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME !== "edge") {
    const { getWorld } = await import("workflow/runtime");
    const world = await getWorld();
    await world.start?.();
  }
}
```

### Create workflow file with 'use workflow' and 'use step' directives

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Create a workflow file in src/ with 'use step' and 'use workflow' directives. The example shows a step function and a workflow function that calls it.

```ts
// src/workflows/example.ts
export async function myStep(data: string) {
  'use step';
  return data.toUpperCase();
}

export async function myWorkflow(input: string) {
  'use workflow';
  const result = await myStep(input);
  return result;
}
```

--------------------------------

### WorkflowAgent example with tool and streaming

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Shows how to create a durable agent with WorkflowAgent, define a step-backed tool, stream model-call output, and limit model calls with stopWhen. The example uses the default model spacexai/grok-4.6 and a plain provider/model string routed through Vercel AI Gateway.

```typescript
import { WorkflowAgent, type ModelCallStreamPart } from "@ai-sdk/workflow";
import { isStepCount, tool } from "ai";
import { getWritable } from "workflow";
import { z } from "zod";

async function lookupData({ query }: { query: string }) {
  "use step";
  // Step functions have full Node.js access
  return `Results for "${query}"`;
}

export async function myAgentWorkflow(userMessage: string) {
  "use workflow";

  const agent = new WorkflowAgent({
    model: "spacexai/grok-4.6",
    instructions: "You are a helpful assistant.",
    tools: {
      lookupData: tool({
        description: "Search for information",
        inputSchema: z.object({ query: z.string() }),
        execute: lookupData,
      }),
    },
  });

  const result = await agent.stream({
    messages: [{ role: "user", content: userMessage }],
    writable: getWritable<ModelCallStreamPart>(),
    stopWhen: isStepCount(10),
  });

  return result.messages;
}
```

### Start a workflow from an API route

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Use start() from an API route to launch a workflow. The function returns a run object with a runId. For a no-arg workflow, call start(noArgWorkflow) without arguments.

```typescript
import { start } from "workflow/api";

// From an API route; works directly
export async function POST() {
  const run = await start(myWorkflow, [arg1, arg2]);
  return Response.json({ runId: run.runId });
}

// No-args workflow
const run = await start(noArgWorkflow);
```

export async function startWorkflowWorld(): Promise<void> {
  await getWorld().start?.();
}

### Static step method with Step and Workflow mode outputs

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/swc-plugin-workflow/spec.md

Static step method example. The input class MyService has a static async method marked with "use step". The Step Mode output registers the method in the global step registry and the class in the class registry. The Workflow Mode output replaces the method body with a call to globalThis[Symbol.for("WORKFLOW_USE_STEP")] and registers the class. Instance methods are not supported.

```javascript
export class MyService {
  static async process(data) {
    "use step";
    return data.value * 2;
  }
}
```

```javascript
/**__internal_workflows{"steps":{"input.js":{"MyService.process":{"stepId":"step//./input//MyService.process"}}},"classes":{"input.js":{"MyService":{"classId":"class//./input//MyService"}}}}*/;
export class MyService {
    static async process(data) {
        return data.value * 2;
    }
}
(function(__wf_fn, __wf_id) {
    var __wf_sym = Symbol.for("@workflow/core//registeredSteps"), __wf_reg = globalThis[__wf_sym] || (globalThis[__wf_sym] = new Map());
    __wf_reg.set(__wf_id, __wf_fn);
    __wf_fn.stepId = __wf_id;
})(MyService.process, "step//./input//MyService.process");
(function(__wf_cls, __wf_id) {
    var __wf_sym = Symbol.for("workflow-class-registry"), __wf_reg = globalThis[__wf_sym] || (globalThis[__wf_sym] = new Map());
    __wf_reg.set(__wf_id, __wf_cls);
    if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(__wf_cls, "classId")) Object.defineProperty(__wf_cls, "classId", { value: __wf_id, writable: false, enumerable: false, configurable: false });
})(MyService, "class//./input//MyService");
```

```javascript
/**__internal_workflows{"steps":{"input.js":{"MyService.process":{"stepId":"step//./input//MyService.process"}}},"classes":{"input.js":{"MyService":{"classId":"class//./input//MyService"}}}}*/;
export class MyService {
}
MyService.process = globalThis[Symbol.for("WORKFLOW_USE_STEP")]("step//./input//MyService.process");
(function(__wf_cls, __wf_id) {
    var __wf_sym = Symbol.for("workflow-class-registry"), __wf_reg = globalThis[__wf_sym] || (globalThis[__wf_sym] = new Map());
    __wf_reg.set(__wf_id, __wf_cls);
    if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(__wf_cls, "classId")) Object.defineProperty(__wf_cls, "classId", { value: __wf_id, writable: false, enumerable: false, configurable: false });
})(MyService, "class//./input//MyService");
```

### Child workflow via step-wrapped start/getRun

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/shared-patterns.md

Shows how to spawn and collect a child workflow using step-wrapped functions. start launches the child and returns a runId; getRun retrieves the run and its return value. The child workflow and step functions are defined in the same file.

```TypeScript
import { getRun, start } from 'workflow/api';

export async function childWorkflow(input: string) {
  'use workflow';
  return await doWork(input);
}

async function doWork(input: string) {
  'use step';
  return { input, status: 'done' as const };
}

async function spawnChild(input: string): Promise<string> {
  'use step';
  const run = await start(childWorkflow, [input]);
  return run.runId;
}

async function collectChild(runId: string) {
  'use step';
  const run = getRun(runId);
  return (await run.returnValue) as { input: string; status: 'done' };
}
```

--------------------------------

### Deterministic server-side resume with createHook and resumeHook

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/shared-patterns.md

Deterministic server-side resume example. The workflow uses `createHook()` with a token, and the POST handler calls `resumeHook()` with the same token pattern. This is the non-Hono variant that uses plain `Request`/`Response`.

```ts
import { createHook } from 'workflow';
import { resumeHook } from 'workflow/api';

export async function approvalWorkflow(orderId: string) {
  'use workflow';

  using approval = createHook<{ approved: boolean }>({
    token: `order:${orderId}:approval`,
  });

  return await approval;
}

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const body = (await request.json()) as {
    orderId: string;
    approved: boolean;
  };

  await resumeHook(`order:${body.orderId}:approval`, {
    approved: body.approved,
  });

  return Response.json({ ok: true });
}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Local World with createWorld() and WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/local.mdx

Programmatic configuration example: create a World with createWorld() and export it from a module, then point WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD at that module. Options passed to createWorld() take precedence over environment variables; baseUrl overrides port if set, and streamFlushIntervalMs is overridden by WORKFLOW_STREAM_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS if set.

```typescript
import { createWorld } from "@workflow/world-local";

export default createWorld({
  dataDir: "./custom-workflow-data",
  port: 5173,
  // baseUrl overrides port if set
  baseUrl: "https://local.example.com:3000",
  recoverActiveRuns: true, // overrides WORKFLOW_LOCAL_RECOVER_ACTIVE_RUNS
  streamFlushIntervalMs: 10, // WORKFLOW_STREAM_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS, if set, overrides this
});
```

```bash
WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD="./my-world.ts"
```

--------------------------------

### Pin a workflow run to a specific region with start()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/docs/content/worlds/v5/vercel.mdx

Use the `region` option in `start()` to pin a run's data and queue dispatch to a specific region, such as `sfo1`. Note that this does not deploy your code; your app must be deployed to that region for execution to happen there.

```typescript
import { start } from "workflow/api";
import { myWorkflow } from "@/workflows/my-workflow";

const run = await start(myWorkflow, [input], { region: "sfo1" });
```

--------------------------------

### Start a child workflow from inside a workflow

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Call start() from within a workflow function to spawn a child run. The child run is created without waiting for it to complete; use childRun.returnValue only when the parent should wait.

```typescript
import { start } from "workflow/api";

export async function parentWorkflow() {
  "use workflow";
  const childRun = await start(childWorkflow, ["some data"]);
  await sleep("1h");
  return { childRunId: childRun.runId };
}
```

--------------------------------

### Self-hosted World interface and startup

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/aws-step-functions.md

Self-hosted runtime requirements: a World interface extending Queue, Streamer, and Storage with an optional start method, and a startup function that calls getWorld().start?.() to run background workers. Required for self-hosted deployments.

```ts
interface World extends Queue, Streamer, Storage {
  start?(): Promise<void>;
}
```

```ts
import { getWorld } from 'workflow/runtime';

export async function startWorkflowWorld(): Promise<void> {
  await getWorld().start?.();
}
```

--------------------------------

### world.streams.get()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Retrieves a readable stream for a given run and stream name, starting from a specified index.

```APIDOC
## world.streams.get()

### Description
Retrieves a readable stream for a given run and stream name, starting from a specified index.

### Method
N/A (SDK method)

### Endpoint
N/A

### Parameters
#### Path Parameters
- **runId** (string) - Required - The ID of the run.
- **name** (string) - Required - The name of the stream.
- **startIndex** (number) - Required - The index to start reading from.

### Request Example
```typescript
const readable = await world.streams.get(runId, name, startIndex);
```

### Response
#### Success Response
- **readable** (ReadableStream) - A readable stream of chunks.

#### Response Example
```typescript
const readable = await world.streams.get(runId, name, startIndex);
```
```

### Example trace output showing out-of-order positions

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/world-sim/README.md

Shows a sample trace output where positions count backwards because the log order disagrees with commit order. The hook owns position 7, the timeout at 8 was committed first, and the branch at 9 went with the timeout. Out-of-order positions are highlighted when color is on.

```text
# 8    +1.0m  wf   wait_completed   @6
# 7    +1.0m  ext    hook_received  @2   token="count:doc-29"
# 9    +1.0m  wf   step_created     @9   settle
```

### Bootstrap database with CLI (npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun)

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/world-postgres/README.md

Run the bootstrap CLI to set up the database. The CLI loads the connection string from WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL, then DATABASE_URL, then defaults to postgres://world:world@localhost:5432/world. Use the command for your package manager.

```bash
# npm
npx --package=@workflow/world-postgres bootstrap
```

```bash

```

```bash
# Yarn
yarn dlx --package @workflow/world-postgres bootstrap
```

```bash
# Bun

```

### Test webhook with resumeWebhook and waitForHook

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Test a workflow that uses a webhook by starting it, waiting for the hook, and resuming it with a Request object. No HTTP server is needed; the hook token is discovered via waitForHook.

```typescript
import { start, resumeWebhook } from "workflow/api";
import { waitForHook } from "@workflow/vitest";

const run = await start(ingestWorkflow, ["ep-1"]);
const hook = await waitForHook(run);  // Discovers the random webhook token
await resumeWebhook(hook.token, new Request("https://example.com/webhook", {
  method: "POST",
  body: JSON.stringify({ event: "order.created" }),
}));
```

### Static workflow method with Workflow mode output

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/swc-plugin-workflow/spec.md

Static workflow method example. The input class JobRunner has a static async method marked with "use workflow". The Workflow Mode output sets the workflowId property and registers the method in globalThis.__private_workflows.

```javascript
export class JobRunner {
  static async runJob(jobId) {
    "use workflow";
    return await processJob(jobId);
  }
}
```

```javascript
/**__internal_workflows{"workflows":{"input.js":{"JobRunner.runJob":{"workflowId":"workflow//./input//JobRunner.runJob"}}}}*/;
export class JobRunner {
    static async runJob(jobId) {
        return await processJob(jobId);
    }
}
JobRunner.runJob.workflowId = "workflow//./input//JobRunner.runJob";
globalThis.__private_workflows.set("workflow//./input//JobRunner.runJob", JobRunner.runJob);
```

--------------------------------

### Get stream in workflow, pass to step

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Shows how to obtain a WritableStream in a workflow function and pass it to a step function for actual I/O. The step function writes data to the stream using getWriter() and write().

```typescript
import { getWritable } from "workflow";

export async function myWorkflow() {
  "use workflow";
  const writable = getWritable();
  await writeData(writable, "hello world");
}

async function writeData(writable: WritableStream, chunk: string) {
  "use step";
  const writer = writable.getWriter();
  try {
    await writer.write(chunk);
  } finally {
    writer.releaseLock();
  }
}
```

### Integration test config with @workflow/vitest plugin

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Vitest configuration for integration tests using the workflow() plugin. Install @workflow/vitest next to workflow and keep them on the same major; the plugin fails the run when its @workflow/core major differs from the app's.

```typescript
// vitest.integration.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";
import { workflow } from "@workflow/vitest";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [workflow()],
  test: {
    include: ["**/*.integration.test.ts"],
    testTimeout: 60_000,
  },
});
```

### Custom class serde implementation with @workflow/serde

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Shows how to implement WORKFLOW_SERIALIZE and WORKFLOW_DESERIALIZE static methods inside a class body using computed property syntax. The class must be in a package with @workflow/serde as a dependency. The example includes a computeDistance method marked with "use step" to keep Node.js-dependent code out of the workflow bundle.

```typescript
import { WORKFLOW_SERIALIZE, WORKFLOW_DESERIALIZE } from "@workflow/serde";

export class Point {
  x: number;
  y: number;

  constructor(x: number, y: number) {
    this.x = x;
    this.y = y;
  }

  // Serialize: return plain data (must be devalue-compatible types only)
  static [WORKFLOW_SERIALIZE](instance: Point) {
    return { x: instance.x, y: instance.y };
  }

  // Deserialize: reconstruct from plain data
  static [WORKFLOW_DESERIALIZE](data: { x: number; y: number }) {
    return new Point(data.x, data.y);
  }

  async computeDistance(other: Point) {
    "use step";
    return Math.sqrt((this.x - other.x) ** 2 + (this.y - other.y) ** 2);
  }
}
```

### Run event-log race repro at historical soak scale

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/AGENTS.md

Run the event-log race repro at the historical soak scale to measure a rate. The default scale (14 runs) is a per-PR regression check, not a rate measurement. This command uses the historical scale with the specified environment variables and skips build and DB setup.

```bash
EVENT_LOG_RACE_REPRO_STEP_STORM_ATTEMPTS=600 \
EVENT_LOG_RACE_REPRO_HOOK_STORM_ATTEMPTS=600 \
EVENT_LOG_RACE_REPRO_ATTEMPTS=200 \
EVENT_LOG_RACE_REPRO_CONCURRENCY=40 \
EVENT_LOG_RACE_REPRO_BUDGET_MS=4500000 \
  pnpm run test:e2e:event-log-race-repro:local --skip-build --skip-db-setup
```

### Integration test for approval workflow with hooks and sleep

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Integration test that starts a workflow, waits for a hook and resumes it, waits for a sleep and wakes it up, then asserts the final result. Uses waitForHook, resumeHook, waitForSleep, and getRun from the workflow API.

```typescript
// approval.integration.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { start, getRun, resumeHook } from "workflow/api";
import { waitForHook, waitForSleep } from "@workflow/vitest";
import { approvalWorkflow } from "./approval";

describe("approvalWorkflow", () => {
  it("should publish when approved", async () => {
    const run = await start(approvalWorkflow, ["doc-123"]);

    // Wait for the hook, then resume it
    await waitForHook(run, { token: "approval:doc-123" });
    await resumeHook("approval:doc-123", { approved: true, reviewer: "alice" });

    // Wait for sleep, then wake it up
    const sleepId = await waitForSleep(run);
    await getRun(run.runId).wakeUp({ correlationIds: [sleepId] });

    const result = await run.returnValue;
    expect(result).toEqual({ status: "published", reviewer: "alice" });
  });
});
```

### Wire up the build command for Vercel

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/nest/README.md

Add a `vercel-build` script to your `package.json` that compiles the app with `nest build` and then emits the Vercel Build Output with `npx @workflow/nest build`. `nest build` (via SWC) compiles your app, including decorator metadata and the workflow client transform, and `@workflow/nest build` bundles the app and workflow functions into `.vercel/output`.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "vercel-build": "nest build && npx @workflow/nest build"
  }
}
```

### resolveData 'none' for status polling and 'all' with hydration

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Shows how to use resolveData to control I/O inclusion. Use 'none' for lightweight status checks; use 'all' (or omit) for full inspection, but always hydrate the data with hydrateResourceIO to get usable values.

```typescript
// Lightweight status check with no I/O loaded
const run = await world.runs.get(runId, { resolveData: 'none' });
console.log(run.status); // 'running' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'cancelled'

// Full inspection: resolveData includes data, hydrateResourceIO deserializes it
const step = await world.steps.get(runId, stepId); // defaults to 'all'
const hydrated = hydrateResourceIO(step, observabilityRevivers);
```

### Print deep link URL for a run

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Commands that print the dashboard deep link and exit without opening a browser or starting a local server. Use --url to print the link, and --json for machine-readable output. The --env flag selects the environment (defaults to production).

```bash
# Vercel run: prints the Vercel dashboard URL for the run
npx workflow inspect run <run_id> --backend vercel --project <project> --team <team> --url
npx workflow web <run_id> --backend vercel --project <project> --team <team> --env preview --url

# Local run: prints the local web UI deep link
npx workflow inspect run <run_id> --url

# Machine-readable: --url --json prints { "url": "..." } to stdout
npx workflow inspect run <run_id> --backend vercel --url --json
```

### Run simulator scenarios with pnpm sim

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/workbench/sim-world/README.md

Run the simulator from the command line. The first command plays all scenarios and prints every event stream. The second filters scenarios by id or name containing "hook". The third runs a single scenario by its id. The command exits non-zero if any scenario misses an expectation or trips a consistency check, so it doubles as the package's integration test.

```bash
pnpm sim                             # play every scenario, print every event stream
pnpm sim hook                        # only scenarios whose id or name contains "hook"
pnpm sim in-flight-after-decision    # one scenario, by id
```

### Next.js instrumentation.ts: start world runtime

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/packages/world-postgres/HOW_IT_WORKS.md

Add this to instrumentation.ts|js in Next.js to ensure workers start before request handling. It dynamically imports the workflow runtime and calls world.start() to begin listening to jobs.

```typescript
// instrumentation.ts

if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME !== "edge") {
  import("workflow/runtime").then(async ({ getWorld }) => {
    // start listening to the jobs.
    const world = await getWorld();
    await world.start?.();
  });
}
```

### Error handling with FatalError, RetryableError, and Promise.allSettled

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Use this TypeScript snippet to handle permanent failures with FatalError (terminates immediately), transient failures with RetryableError (retries with optional retryAfter delay), and parallel steps with mixed criticality using Promise.allSettled. The example shows how to check the critical result and rethrow a FatalError if it fails.

```typescript
import { FatalError, RetryableError } from "workflow";

// Permanent failure, so the workflow terminates
throw new FatalError("Invalid input: missing required field");

// Transient failure, so it will retry
throw new RetryableError("API rate limited", { retryAfter: "5m" });

// Mixed criticality parallel execution
const results = await Promise.allSettled([
  criticalStep(data),    // Must succeed
  optionalStep(data),    // OK to fail
  enrichmentStep(data),  // OK to fail
]);
const [critical, optional, enrichment] = results;
if (critical.status === "rejected") throw new FatalError(critical.reason);
```

### Hono app boundary for starting refund workflow

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-to-workflow-sdk/references/aws-step-functions.md

Hono app boundary that exposes a POST /api/refunds/start endpoint, parses the refundId from the request body, starts the refundWorkflow with that ID, and returns the runId in the JSON response.

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { start } from 'workflow/api';
import { refundWorkflow } from '../workflows/refund';

const app = new Hono();

app.post('/api/refunds/start', async (c) => {
  const body = (await c.req.json()) as { refundId: string };
  const run = await start(refundWorkflow, [body.refundId]);
  return c.json({ runId: run.runId });
});

export default app;
```

### world.steps.list()

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/workflow/SKILL.md

Lists steps for a given run with pagination and optional data resolution.

```APIDOC
## world.steps.list()

### Description
Lists steps for a given run with pagination and optional data resolution.

### Method
N/A (SDK method)

### Endpoint
N/A

### Parameters
#### Query Parameters
- **runId** (string) - Required - The ID of the run (top-level, not inside pagination).
- **pagination** (object) - Optional - Pagination object with nested cursor: `{ pagination: { cursor } }`.
- **resolveData** (string) - Optional - 'all' (default) or 'none' to include or exclude I/O data.

### Request Example
```typescript
const { data, cursor } = await world.steps.list({ runId, pagination: { cursor }, resolveData: 'all' | 'none' });
```

### Response
#### Success Response
- **data** (array) - List of steps.
- **cursor** (string) - Pagination cursor for next page.

#### Response Example
```typescript
const { data, cursor } = await world.steps.list({ runId, pagination: { cursor }, resolveData: 'all' });
```
```

### experimental_setAttributes renamed to setAttributes

Source: https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/main/skills/migrating-workflow-v4-to-v5/SKILL.md

The experimental_setAttributes export was renamed to setAttributes in v5. Update imports accordingly. The options type is now SetAttributesOptions, and the attributes option on start() is unchanged.

```typescript
// v4
import { experimental_setAttributes } from 'workflow';

// v5
import { setAttributes } from 'workflow';
```

### World interface for self-hosted runtimes

}
